title: Turin — forty-five minutes, one kilometre
learning_goal: Find three things at Porta Nuova without being told where to point — the name, the clock, and the fact that the rails end here — and learn that the world's oldest museum of ancient Egypt is a walk away from a man on his way to Egypt.

narration.script:
Twenty-five to seven in the morning, in Turin. Fogg has forty-five minutes. Three things to find. First: read the name across the front of the station. Second: find the clock. Third: look at how the building closes the end of the square — the rails stop here, and everyone has to turn round.

Torino Porta Nuova. When Fogg waited here, the station was four years old. And the city had just lost something too: Turin was the capital of Italy from 1861 to 1865, and had been an ordinary city again for seven years.

Now the pin. About nine hundred metres in that direction — you cannot see it from here — is the oldest museum in the world devoted only to ancient Egypt. It was founded in 1824. Fogg is on his way to Egypt. He has forty-five minutes.

production_notes: SEGMENT 7 (90 s, fill 70 %, ceiling 150 words; it spends 134). STOP-AND-LOOK #1 OF 2 — and two is the whole chapter's budget (D6). There is a real task with three named finds, all said out loud, which is what earns Street View here: no walking, no route, no waypoint transport. The stop's coordinates live on the M-216 media entry, exactly as Day-1 scene 15 does since D6; there is deliberately no `interaction.route`, because a route of one is transport grammar. Player: Maps EMBED (drag to look), free SKU, nothing billable. THE CAMERA TRACK IS THE FILM'S VERSION and the player's guided version: six cues, each within 3 s of the overlay that names the same thing. THE MUSEO EGIZIO BEARING IS RECOMPUTED: the rundown says 060°, but F-104 -> F-105 is 033° at 865 m and this camera point -> F-105 is 035° at about 710 m, so the cue uses look_at (which the runtime aims from wherever the pano actually is) and the narration says 'about nine hundred metres' — F-87's own 'about 1 km' measured from the station, not from the pavement we are standing on. WHY THE PAYOFF IS IN `script` AND NOT `after_script`: the player speaks `after_script` only when a graded interaction resolves; a `look` scene has no options, so an after_script here would never be heard and the Egypt joke — the whole reason for the stop — would be lost. It is in `script`, after the finds, and the 30 s look budget follows the words. Known engine stall, inherited from Day-1 scene 15: `tick()`'s needsInput test exempts only `walk` on a streetview scene, so this scene waits for ▶ rather than auto-advancing. THE SALA GONIN (F-86) is a caption candidate only and is NOT in this scene: public access is unverified (fact sheet gap) and we do not send anyone anywhere we have not checked. LINEAR CUT (70 s): a slow pan over the same view following the camera cues, the words unchanged, the guide naming what the player-traveller would have found — D6's own adaptation rule — then M-243 as the insert on 'the rails stop here'. M-204 (Turin 1911) is unwatched and must not be cut in on anyone's word.

review.notes: Scene Developer + Narrator draft 2026-08-27. CUE/OVERLAY TIMINGS, and the sentence each is timed against: 0 the whole front, under 'Twenty-five to seven in the morning, and Turin'; 14 tight on the name, under 'read the name across the front of the station'; 30 the clock, under 'Second: find the clock'; 44 wide, under 'look at how the building closes the end of the square'; 62 turn towards the museum, under 'Now the pin. About nine hundred metres that way'; 78 settle back, under 'He has forty-five minutes.' Every pin and caption has a cue within 3 s. The two stills are `use: linear` and are not on the player's clock — they are the fallback and the film. GLOSS: the chip glosses 'Torino', which the guide says out loud at ~30 s. The rundown's 'il binario' chip is CUT: the guide never says the word, and a chip may not gloss a word the traveller does not hear. QA MUST CONFIRM the pano exists at 45.063200,7.679200 (the founder's key is referrer-restricted, so nobody could check from the studio) and that the station name and the clock are legible at the authored zooms.
